# A ball that contains two balls, one-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_hull_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball that contains the union of two balls, $X$ the ball of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$; the empty set and the whole line included:

$$Z \supseteq X \cup Y.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X.hull(Y)` | `Ball<T, 1>`, `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | contains both, not claimed the smallest; with an empty operand, the other as it is; `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result, the ball $Z$ of center $c_z$ and radius $r_z$, is a canonical ball.
- $Z$ contains every member of $X$ and every member of $Y$.
- $Z$ is empty exactly when $X$ and $Y$ both are; when $X$ is empty, $Z$ is $Y$ as it is (the same limbs); when $Y$ is empty and $X$ is not, $Z$ is $X$ as it is.
- Not claimed: that $Z$ is the smallest such ball.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_hull_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallHull.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallHull.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_hull_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_hull_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** both balls to intervals, their hull, back to a ball (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_hull_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_hull_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`ball_to_interval_1`](ball_to_interval_1.md), [`interval_hull_1`](interval_hull_1.md), [`interval_to_ball_1`](interval_to_ball_1.md).

```
# A ball with a one-limb center that contains two such balls (milestone2.md, "One enclosure
# interface", "Hull, intersection and split of balls"): both balls to intervals (ball_to_interval_1,
# the smallest intervals of T that contain them), the hull of the intervals (interval_hull_1), back to
# a ball (interval_to_ball_1). If X is empty Y is returned as it is, and if Y is empty and X is not, X
# (the same limbs), by the tests of the radii (a NaN radius is the empty ball); the composition alone
# would return it converted twice. Two empty balls give Y, whose NaNs need not be X's, which is why
# the second clause has its condition. The whole line gives the whole line through the conversions.
# The selects choose the composition when both operands are not empty (qx, qy), the case the scalar
# printer puts first. Not claimed: the smallest such ball.

(xl, xu) = ball_to_interval_1(cx, rx)
(yl, yu) = ball_to_interval_1(cy, ry)
(zl, zu) = interval_hull_1(xl, xu, yl, yu)
(c, r)   = interval_to_ball_1(zl, zu)
qx       = eq(rx, rx)
qy       = eq(ry, ry)
ca       = select(qy, c, cx)
ra       = select(qy, r, rx)
cz       = select(qx, ca, cy)
rz       = select(qx, ra, ry)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_hull_1)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats | 3 420 868 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
